guidance.heading: Choose by how many falls the load hangs on
guidance.body: On a single fall, an ordinary six- or eight-strand rope tries to unlay under load and spins the hook. Rotation-resistant ropes lay their strand layers in opposite directions so the torques cancel. 35Wx7 turns the least and suits tower cranes and high lifts; 18x7 and 19x7 cost less and suit overhead cranes, electric hoists and winches.

standards.heading: Constructions and grades
standards.body: The tables give minimum breaking loads by wire grade (1570 to 2160 N/mm²). They are test loads: the working load is the breaking load divided by the design factor your crane or hoist standard requires. Every rope ships with the manufacturer’s test certificate.

items.q: What is the difference between non-rotating and rotation-resistant rope?
items.a: The terms are used for the same ropes. 35Wx7-class ropes turn the least and are often called non-rotating; 18x7 and 19x7 are rotation-resistant.

items.q: Can I fit a swivel to a rotation-resistant rope?
items.a: Only where the crane maker allows it. A swivel lets some constructions unlay and lose strength.

products.title: 35Wx7 Rotation-Resistant Wire Rope — 10–48 mm
products.descriptionShort: 35Wx7 rotation-resistant (non-rotating) steel wire rope in 20 sizes, 10 mm to 48 mm, wire grades 1670 to 2160. Bright or galvanized. Indus part numbers.
products.descriptionLong:
Multi-strand rotation-resistant wire rope: 35 strands of seven wires in three layers, the outer layer laid opposite to the inner ones so the torque of each layer cancels the other. Under load it turns very little, which is what a single-fall hoist, a tower crane or a deep lift needs, where a six-strand rope would spin the load and unlay itself.

Sizes

20 sizes, 10 mm to 48 mm, in five wire grades: 1670, 1770, 1870, 1960 and 2160 N/mm². Bright (ungalvanized) or galvanized, right-hand or left-hand ordinary lay. Every size has its own Indus part number in the table below.

Minimum breaking loads are the manufacturer's published figures for each wire grade. Every batch ships with the mill test certificate, which is the figure to design to. They are test loads, not working loads: the working load follows from the design factor your standard or application requires.

Choosing and handling

Use a rotation-resistant rope where the load hangs on one fall or the lift is high. Keep the fleet angle small and the sheaves to the rope's recommended diameter: multi-layer ropes are sensitive to crushing and to being turned on a swivel. Cut it only after seizing both sides, so the layers do not shift.

Ordering

Quote the Indus part number from the size table, or send the diameter, construction, wire grade, finish and length you need. Rope is supplied cut to length or on reels, with the manufacturer's test certificate.

faqs.question: What does 35Wx7 mean?
faqs.answer: 35 strands of 7 wires each. The strands are laid in layers in opposite directions, so the rope resists turning under load. The W refers to the Warrington layout of the strands.

faqs.question: Where is rotation-resistant rope used?
faqs.answer: Tower and mobile crane hoists, single-fall lifts, deep shafts and any lift where the load must not spin. Use it where a six- or eight-strand rope would turn the block.

faqs.question: Which wire grade should I order?
faqs.answer: Match the grade the crane or hoist maker specifies. A higher grade carries more for the same diameter; the table lists the minimum breaking load for every grade.

products.title: 18x7 Rotation-Resistant Wire Rope — Fibre or Steel Core, 6–50 mm
products.descriptionShort: 18x7 rotation-resistant wire rope with a fibre core or a steel strand core, 27 sizes from 6 mm to 50 mm. Grades 1770 and 1960 in the table; 1670, 1870 and 2160 on request.
products.descriptionLong:
Eighteen strands of seven wires in two layers: six inner strands laid one way around the core, twelve outer strands laid the other. The opposing layers keep the rope from spinning under load, at a lower cost and with more flexibility than a 35-strand rope. Used on overhead cranes, electric hoists, winches and guying where the load hangs on one fall.

Sizes

27 sizes, 6 mm to 50 mm, with a fibre core (FC) or an independent wire strand core (IWS). The table gives weights for both cores and minimum breaking loads for the 1770 and 1960 grades; 1670, 1870 and 2160 grades are made to order. Bright or galvanized.

Minimum breaking loads are the manufacturer's published figures, checked size by size against a second maker's table. They are test loads, not working loads: the working load follows from the design factor your standard or application requires.

Fibre or steel core?

A fibre core is lighter and more flexible. A steel core carries about 6% more for the same diameter and resists crushing on a multi-layer drum. Choose the core the equipment maker specifies.

Ordering

Quote the Indus part number from the size table, or send the diameter, construction, wire grade, finish and length you need. Rope is supplied cut to length or on reels, with the manufacturer's test certificate.
